requirement: Create a POST /orders endpoint returning 202 Accepted, scheduling BackgroundTasks.add_task(process_order, order_id), updating in-memory ORDERS_DB status from pending to processed, recording audit log, and validating quantity > 0 with lowercase email normalization.
skeleton: FastAPI route with BackgroundTasks parameter, in-memory state transition, and audit logging.

rationale.teaches: An accept-then-process endpoint: 202 status, add_task with a real callable, a state transition the worker performs, unconditional audit logging, and a quantity constraint that allows one.
rationale.why: Background work is invisible in the response, so a generated route can return 202 while nothing ever runs. The fixture inspects the in-memory state after the request, which is the only way to prove the task was scheduled and completed.

candidates.why_wrong: The endpoint answers 200 instead of 202, so the client assumes the order was processed synchronously.
add_task receives None instead of process_order, so the background task crashes and the order stays pending.
The worker never sets status to processed, so every order stays pending forever.
Only partner.com customers are audit-logged, so every other order is processed without a trace.
quantity must exceed 1, so a single-item order is rejected with 422.
